samples.text:
The pie charts shows the kinds of jobs that working women did in one country in 1970 and 2020.

In 1970, the most common job for women was clerical, it was 32%. Manufacturing was 21%. Retail and sales and domestic and care was both 17%. Professional jobs was 10% and managerial jobs was the lowest with only 3%. So clerical and manufacturing was more than half of all women jobs at that time.

In 2020, professional jobs increased very much to 31% and it became the largest group. Managerial jobs also increased from 3% to 15%, so it was five times more. On the other hand, clerical jobs fell to 17% and manufacturing dropped a lot to only 5%. Retail and sales decrease a little to 14%, and domestic and care went up slightly to 18%.

Overall, in 1970 many women worked in clerical and manufacturing jobs, but in 2020 more women had professional and managerial jobs. Domestic and care was almost the same in both year.
samples.why: Key changes reported with accurate figures · overview placed at the end · mechanical, repetitive linking · adequate vocabulary with some awkward choices · several agreement, tense and plural errors that do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
The pie charts compare the occupations of working women in one country in 1970 and 2020.

Overall, there was a significant shift from clerical and manufacturing work towards professional and managerial roles over the fifty-year period. Professional occupations replaced clerical work as the most common type of employment for women.

In 1970, almost a third of working women (32%) were employed in clerical positions, and a further 21% worked in manufacturing. Retail and sales and domestic and care work each accounted for 17%, while professional jobs made up 10%. Only 3% of women held managerial posts.

By 2020, the proportion of women in professional jobs had more than tripled to 31%, and the share in managerial roles had risen fivefold to 15%. In contrast, clerical work fell to 17%, and manufacturing saw the sharpest decline, dropping from 21% to just 5%. The remaining categories changed very little, with retail and sales decreasing slightly to 14% and domestic and care increasing marginally to 18%. As a result, domestic and care work became the second largest category in 2020.
samples.why: Clear overview of the main shift · key features highlighted with accurate figures and correct multiples · logical paragraphing · good range of linkers · appropriate less common vocabulary · mostly error-free sentences.

samples.text:
The charts illustrate how the occupations of working women in one country changed between 1970 and 2020.

The overall pattern is a marked movement away from clerical and manufacturing work towards higher-level professional and managerial positions, with professional work becoming the most common occupation by 2020. Domestic and care work, by contrast, remained remarkably stable.

In 1970, clerical jobs employed the largest share of working women, at 32%, and manufacturing accounted for a further 21%, so together these two sectors employed more than half of the female workforce. Retail and sales and domestic and care work each represented 17%, whereas professional occupations made up only 10% and managerial roles a mere 3%.

Fifty years later, professional work had risen to 31%, more than three times its earlier level, and the share of women in managerial positions had increased fivefold to 15%. Meanwhile, clerical work had almost halved to 17%, and manufacturing had undergone the steepest decline, shrinking to just 5% of female employment. Retail and sales fell only slightly, to 14%, and domestic and care work edged up by a single point to 18%, making it the second largest category.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected · clear, well-placed overview · accurate, selective comparison with correct derived values · cohesion managed naturally · precise, varied vocabulary · wide range of structures, error-free.
